title: Second-filtration spectral data with the total cohomology image filtration
statement: Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be an additive left exact functor between Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-left-exact-additive, def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. Let K be a bounded-below cochain complex in $\mathcal A$, and let $a:K\to I$ be a bicomplex augmentation into a double complex with complex degree $s\in\mathbf Z$ and resolution degree $r\in\mathbf N$. Assume that I vanishes for $s<b$ for some integer b, every $I^{s,r}$ is injective and every row augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Set $T=\operatorname{Tot}((F(I)\text{ extended by zero})^{\mathrm{flip}})$ using [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-presentation]. There exist a filtration L of T by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration], a cohomological spectral sequence E starting at page zero, page-zero identifications with the degreewise graded pieces, and signed identifications $E_1^{s,r}\cong R^rF(K^s)$. The steps of L equal the second-filtration image sums [def-sp-double-complex-total]. The page-zero differential is that of the graded complex; the terms at every page $t\ge1$ are the cokernels of the inclusions $B_t\subseteq Z_t$ [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. Under the signed first-page identifications, $d_1$ is $R^rF(d_K)$, and $E_1^{p,q}=0$ for $q<0$. For every family of objects $Y^n$ and isomorphisms $c_n:H^n(T)\cong Y^n$, there is a finite decreasing filtration H on each $Y^n$ whose p-th step is the direct image along $c_n$ of $\operatorname{im}(H^n(L^pT)\to H^n(T))$. For each p,n there is $t\ge1$ such that all page-r terms at $(p,n-p)$ for $r\ge t$ are isomorphic to $\operatorname{gr}^pH(Y^n)$. This statement asserts no derived-complex interpretation of $H^n(T)$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: second filtration, signed row identifications and total-cohomology convergence (Stacks 0130 and 0132)

proof.text: Write J for the flipped, extended, F-mapped bicomplex. On each diagonal the only nonzero summands have resolution degree nonnegative and complex degree at least b. The second-filtration step is the sum of inclusions indexed by complex degree in [p,n]. The total differential preserves or raises that degree, hence these subobjects assemble into a decreasing filtration L by subcomplexes. Its steps in degree n are top for $p\le b$ and bottom for $p>n$, including n<b. This construction does not require one upper filtration bound for the entire complex.

Use [lem-sp-filtered-complex-associated-spectral-sequence-construction] for the filtered total. Its page-zero differential and its $Z_t/B_t$ description give the first two compatibility clauses. The graded complex at complex degree s is the row $F(I^{s,\bullet})$ placed in total degrees s+r. Its cohomology is zero for r<0; for r nonnegative the injective-resolution comparison with right derived functors identifies it with $R^rF(K^s)$. Naturality of that comparison identifies the map induced by $I^{s,\bullet}\to I^{s+1,\bullet}$ with $R^rF(d_K)$. Stacks 0130 gives the second-filtration sign $(-1)^r$. Multiply the identification at (s,r) by $(-1)^{rs}$; the ratio of the factors at s+1 and s is $(-1)^r$, cancelling the sign.

Fix total degree n. In the cycle and boundary formulas, choose t so large that $p+t>n+1$ and $p-t+1\le b$. For every $r\ge t$, $F^{p+r}T^{n+1}=0$ and $F^{p-r+1}T^{n-1}=T^{n-1}$. Thus $Z_r$ is the image of the actual cycles in $F^pT^n$, and $B_r$ the image of the actual boundaries in $F^pT^n$. Their quotient is the cokernel of the successive inclusion in the image filtration on $H^n(T)$. The steps are top at b and bottom at n+1, so this cohomology filtration is finite. This proves degreewise stabilization and the stationary graded-piece comparison, as in Stacks 0132.

Given $c_n$, take the direct image of each step of the total-cohomology filtration along $(c_n).\mathrm{hom}$. Functoriality of subobject direct image gives antitonicity. Since $c_n$ is an isomorphism, this operation preserves top, bottom and cokernels of step inclusions. It therefore gives a finite filtration with the required step formula and carries the stationary graded-piece isomorphisms to Y.
